intl: UK LOLER 1998 (6-monthly accessories), BS EN 13155, EN 13889, EN 1677, EN 818, EN 1492, ISO 4309; BS 7121

t: Hand & Power Tools (incl. Abrasive Wheels, Pneumatic & Powder-Actuated Tools)
purpose: Prevent cuts, eye injuries, electrocution, disc bursts, kickback, hand-arm vibration and dust/noise harm from tools.
scope: Hand tools (hammers, chisels, spanners, knives), electric tools (drills, grinders, saws, breakers), pneumatic tools, hydraulic tools, powder-actuated (cartridge) tools, battery tools, bench grinders, chop saws.
hazards: Angle-grinder disc burst (wrong RPM/size, damaged disc), kickback, cutting with grinding disc, guard removed
Electric shock (damaged cable/plug, wet), no RCD
Eye injuries from chips/sparks; hand injuries; HAV; noise; silica dust from cutting
Pneumatic: hose whip, compressed-air injection; powder-actuated: ricochet/through-penetration
pre: Tool register with inspection colour-code (quarterly) and PAT (3-monthly site / annual workshop); defective tools quarantined
Right tool for the task; manufacturer manuals available; abrasive wheels stored dry, flat, and mounted only by trained persons after ring test; wheel RPM ≥ tool RPM
Guards fitted and working (grinder guard covers ≥ 180°, saw retractable guard); side handles; dead-man triggers; anti-restart on bench tools
RCD (30 mA) on all electric tools; 110 V CTE or double-insulated; cables elevated; no taped joints
Vibration data per tool; trigger-time limits; job rotation; anti-vibration handles
steps: Pre-use check by user: body, cable/plug, guard, switch, disc/blade condition and rating, hose couplings and whip-checks, battery/charger condition; tag out if defective.
Set up: secure workpiece (clamp/vice), stable footing, exclusion for sparks/chips, fire precautions and hot-work permit where sparks near combustibles, dust control (water or LEV) for concrete/stone.

Operate within design: correct disc (cutting vs grinding), no overreach, two hands, let tool reach full speed before contact, do not force; keep cords away from cutting path; allow disc to stop before putting down.
Pneumatic: ≤ 30 psi (2 bar) for cleaning with chip guards, never towards people or clothing; whip-checks at every coupling; isolate and bleed before changing bits.
Powder-actuated: licensed operator only; sequential-action tool; check substrate (no through-penetration), no use near flammables, cartridges stored locked, misfire wait 30 s then unload.
Hand tools: chisels dressed (no mushrooming), handles tight, knives retractable, insulated tools for electrical work, non-sparking in flammable areas, carry in holsters not pockets.
Bench grinders: work-rest ≤ 3 mm gap, tongue guard ≤ 6 mm, eye shield; ring-test wheels; dress regularly.
Battery tools: charge on non-combustible surface, use manufacturer charger, do not charge damaged packs, store cool; Li-ion fire response (water in quantity, do not reuse).
Record inspections; retrain on incidents; report near-misses (disc bursts, kickbacks).
ppe: Safety glasses + face shield for grinding/cutting, gloves (not near rotating parts where entanglement), hearing protection, FFP2/P3 for dust, anti-vibration gloves (limited), safety boots
stop: Disc damaged, wrong size/RPM or cutting disc used for grinding
Dry cutting of concrete without dust control
records: Tool register, inspection colour-code log, PAT records, abrasive-wheel mounting training, powder-actuated licences, vibration exposure log

Sch. II PELs (silica) for cutting; OSH Code s.6

tn: TN Factories Rules 1950; TN BOCW Rules

intl: UK PUWER 1998; HSG17 Safety in the use of abrasive wheels; Control of Vibration at Work Regs 2005; EN 62841; ILO CoP Construction

t: Tower Cranes & Overhead (EOT) Cranes – Erection, Operation, Inspection, Dismantling
purpose: Prevent tower-crane collapse, overturning, load drops, collisions and crush injuries, and EOT crane failures in factories.
scope: Self-erecting, hammerhead, luffing and internal-climbing tower cranes; EOT/gantry cranes in workshops and warehouses; monorails and jib cranes by analogy.
hazards: Foundation/tie failure, overload, out-of-service wind, erection/climbing errors, mast bolt failure, slew-ring failure
Collision between cranes/jibs and with structures; loads over public roads
Falls during erection/maintenance; crush between counter-jib and structure
EOT: limit-switch failure (two-blocking), brake failure, rail misalignment, pendant/remote faults, persons on walkways
pre: Tower crane: foundation and tie design by manufacturer/engineer with ground investigation; erection method statement; wind data and manufacturer limits (in-service typically 9–10 m/s at hook; out-of-service free-slew with jib unloaded); lightning protection; anti-collision/zone-limiting on multi-crane sites; load-moment indicator, limit switches, anemometer, slew/trolley limits

Test & thorough examination by competent person after each erection/climb and every 12 months (state rules) — certificate in cab; daily operator checks; weekly/monthly inspection schedule (bolts torque, ties, slew ring, ropes, brakes)
Operator certification/medical (vision, no vertigo), rescue-from-cab plan, cab access ladders with rest platforms/fall arrest; communication (radio) with signallers

EOT: IS 3177/IS 807 design; limit switches (upper hoist, cross/long travel), brakes, overload device, rail stops, warning horn, isolator, inspection access, 125% load test after major repair, 12-monthly examination
Public interface: loads not over public roads/occupied areas unless engineered exclusion and permission; night lighting/aviation warning if near airports (AAI NOC for height)
steps: Erect/climb/dismantle only with manufacturer-trained crew under supervisor; exclusion zone; weather within limits; sequence per manual (no shortcuts); torque bolts to spec; independent check before load test.
Daily pre-use: structure/ties visual, ropes, hook latch, LMI/limits functional test, anemometer, brakes; log; stop if any defect.
Operate within load chart (radius); trial lift; no side pull/dragging; loads with tag lines; banksman/signaller for blind lifts; slow slewing near structures.
Multi-crane sites: priority rules, anti-collision set and verified, communication protocol; no jib overlap without zoning.

Weather: stop lifting at manufacturer wind limit (≈ 9–10 m/s; lower for large-surface loads); lightning – stop and leave cab; cyclone/storm warning – put crane out of service (jib free-slew, hook up, trolley in, power off) per manual; after storm – inspection before use.
Night/idle: hook raised, no load left suspended, power isolated, access locked; no unauthorised climbing.
Maintenance at height under WAH rules (harness to designated anchors), isolation of slew/hoist; replacement of ropes/limit switches by trained persons; re-test after repair.

EOT operations: authorised operators only; pre-use checks; sound horn before travel; no riding on hook/load; never leave load suspended; keep persons clear of load path; stack loads stable; lockout for maintenance on crane rails with rail stops; two-crane tandem lifts only under lift plan.
Inspection records and certificates filed; competent person examination every 12 months; operator refresher every 2–3 years.
ppe: Helmet with chin strap, harness for erection/maintenance, gloves, boots, hi-vis; radios
stop: Tie/bolt looseness, unusual noise or movement
Load path over persons/public without control
records: Erection method statement, foundation/tie design, competent-person test certificates, daily/weekly/monthly inspections, operator certificates, lift plans, anti-collision settings, storm shutdown records, EOT inspection & load test

india: Factories Act s.29 via state rules (12-monthly test & examination; register); BOCW Central Rules 1998 & KA/TN BOCW Rules (lifting appliances – test after erection, certificate, operator); IS 13367 Pt 1, IS 4573, IS 3177, IS 807; AAI height NOC; CEA clearances
OSH Code s.6, s.11 (crane collapse = dangerous occurrence, 12 h notice)

intl: BS 7121-5 (tower cranes), BS 7121-1; BS EN 14439; UK CPA tower crane guidance; LOLER; ILO CoP Construction

t: Forklifts, Powered Industrial Trucks, Warehousing & Racking
purpose: Prevent tip-overs, pedestrian strikes, falling loads, racking collapse and charging-area incidents in warehouses, yards and factories.
scope: Counterbalance (diesel/LPG/electric), reach trucks, pallet trucks, order pickers, telehandlers, tow tractors; pallet racking, cantilever racks, mezzanines, block stacking, loading docks.
hazards: Tip-over (speed, turns with raised load, slopes, overload, uneven ground), operator ejection without seat belt
Pedestrians struck in aisles/doorways/reversing; falling loads from high racks; racking impact damage and collapse
Battery charging: hydrogen explosion, acid burns; LPG cylinder changeover leaks; CO from engines indoors
Falls from forks/platforms; dock edge falls; trailer creep during loading
pre: Operator training with practical evaluation; authorisation card; refresher every 3 years and after incident; medical fitness; RTO licence if on public road
Truck: capacity plate (load centre 600 mm/24 in), attachment de-rating, daily pre-use checklist, horn, lights, reversing alarm/blue spot, seat belt, overhead guard, mast chains; maintenance records
Traffic plan: segregated pedestrian walkways, crossings, mirrors at blind corners, speed limits (≤ 8–10 km/h indoors), one-way aisles, no-go zones, lighting

Racking: designed and installed per supplier; SWL load notices per bay; column guards; floor flatness; inspections – weekly by staff, annual by expert (EN 15635/SEMA); damage classified green/amber/red; sprinkler clearance ≥ 450 mm

Charging/LPG: dedicated ventilated room (hydrogen < 1%), no ignition, eyewash, spill kit, insulated tools, PPE; LPG cylinders stored outdoors, changeover outdoors with gloves/goggles; CO monitoring for engine trucks indoors
steps: Pre-use inspection and log; defective truck tagged out.
Drive with forks low (150–200 mm), tilted back; slow at corners/doorways, sound horn; look in direction of travel; reverse with load blocking view; use spotter in congested areas.
Load within capacity for the load centre; stable, strapped/wrapped pallets; never raise persons on forks (only approved platform with harness anchor); no passengers.
Stacking: square to racks, raise/lower only when stopped and straight; check beam SWL; no overhang; damaged pallets not stacked high.
Slopes: drive with load uphill; no turning on ramps; dock plates secured; trailer wheels chocked and keys with loader (vehicle restraint) before entry.
Parking: forks down, neutral, brake, key out; not blocking exits/fire equipment.
Racking damage: report any impact; amber (reduce/inspect) and red (unload immediately, isolate) actions; repair by supplier parts only; re-inspect.

Charging: park in charging bay, switch off, ventilation on, no smoking; connect/disconnect with charger off; check electrolyte with PPE; LPG changeover procedure; refuelling diesel outdoors with engine off.
Housekeeping: aisles clear, no damaged pallets, spill clean-up; lighting maintained.
Incident/near-miss reporting; weekly racking walk; annual expert inspection; audit of operator authorisations.
ppe: Hi-vis, safety boots, helmet where overhead risk, gloves/goggles/apron for batteries & LPG
stop: Seat belt not worn / overhead guard missing
Pedestrian in aisle with truck moving loads
records: Operator authorisations & training, daily checks, maintenance, racking inspection reports (weekly/annual), damage register, charging-area checks, incident log

OSH Code s.6; design/operation per ASME B56.1 / ISO 3691 (no dedicated Indian forklift safety code)

purpose: Prevent electrocution and arc-flash injuries during switching, isolation, testing and maintenance on HT (≥ 1 kV) and large LT systems.
scope: HT switchgear (11/22/33/66/110 kV), transformers, ring main units, cable terminations, capacitor banks, busbars, LT PCC/MCC above 240 V, generator paralleling panels, battery/UPS rooms, solar inverter stations.
hazards: Shock from induced/back-feed/capacitive charge; failure to earth; wrong-bay isolation
Arc flash from racking breakers, live testing, loose connections, animal ingress, moisture
Transformer oil fire; SF6 decomposition products; battery hydrogen
Falls in cable trenches; manual handling of heavy breakers
pre: Single-line diagram current and displayed; equipment labelled uniquely; switching schedule written and checked by second person
Arc-flash study (IEEE 1584) with labels (incident energy, boundaries, PPE category); NFPA 70E approach boundaries applied

Test equipment: proved HV detector/discharge rod rated for voltage, portable earths (rated), insulating mats/gloves (IS 4770 class per voltage) tested 6-monthly, lockable isolators, caution/danger boards
Statutory: CEIG approval before energising new/modified HT installations; periodic inspection; competent-person authorisation list; CEA regs on clearances and working
Emergency: fire extinguishers (CO2/clean agent), eyewash in battery rooms, rescue hooks, first-aiders trained in electrical shock CPR/AED, emergency lighting
steps: Plan: switching program and permit (HT PTW) with isolation points, earthing, boundaries; brief team; confirm utility shutdown (BESCOM/TANGEDCO) and no back-feed from generators/solar.
Isolate at all sources (incoming, bus-coupler, generator, inverter); rack out/open isolators; lock and tag; discharge capacitive charge.

Prove dead with a tested detector on all phases (test the tester before and after); apply portable earths at point of work (and both sides for cables); hang 'MEN AT WORK' boards; mark safe zone with barriers.
Issue permit to work; authorised person stays on site; no work outside the defined zone; adjacent live equipment screened/locked.

Live work (only where unavoidable – testing, thermography): energised work permit, qualified persons, arc-rated PPE by label category, remote racking/operation where possible, no jewellery, stand to the side when operating.
Transformer/oil: handle oil as flammable; bund/soak pit; fire wall; gas monitoring for SF6 rooms; cable trenches covered and fire-stopped; vermin proofing.
Restore: remove earths and tools (count), withdraw persons, cancel permit, close/lock enclosures, test insulation if opened, energise in sequence with remote operation where possible.
Maintenance: thermography annually, insulation resistance/dissolved gas analysis per plan, relay testing, breaker servicing per OEM; records for Electrical Inspector.
Access control: locked, signed, authorised entry only; housekeeping; no storage.
Electrical accident: isolate, rescue with insulated means, CPR/AED, call 108; report to Electrical Inspector within 48 h (Form A), fatal – immediately.
ppe: Arc-rated clothing per label (cal/cm²), arc-rated face shield/hood, insulated gloves (class per kV) with leather protectors, insulated footwear, helmet (non-vented, Class E), hearing protection for arc; insulated tools
stop: Cannot prove dead or earths cannot be applied
Switching schedule not checked by second person
Arc-flash PPE unavailable for the labelled category
records: Switching schedules, HT permits, earth application register, authorised-person list, arc-flash study/labels, insulating PPE test records, CEIG approvals/inspections, maintenance/test records, accident reports

t: Battery Rooms, Energy Storage (Li-ion), Solar PV Installations & EV Charging
purpose: Prevent fire/explosion, electric shock, chemical burns and falls associated with battery systems, rooftop/ground solar PV and EV charging infrastructure.
scope: Lead-acid/VRLA UPS and telecom batteries; lithium-ion BESS and forklift packs; rooftop and ground-mount PV (construction, O&M, cleaning); inverters/DC systems; EV charging stations in plants and parking.
hazards: Lead-acid: hydrogen accumulation/explosion, sulphuric acid burns, short-circuit arcs from tools/jewellery
Li-ion: thermal runaway, toxic/flammable off-gas (HF, CO), re-ignition, propagation; damaged/over-charged cells
PV: DC arcs (no zero-crossing), shock from live strings in daylight (cannot be switched off at modules), rooftop falls/fragile roofs, module fires, lightning
EV charging: cable damage, RCD/DC leakage, vehicle fires in enclosed car parks
pre: Battery rooms: ventilation keeps H2 < 1% (25% LEL), no ignition sources, acid-resistant floor/bund, eyewash/shower, insulated tools, PPE, signage; Li-ion BESS per NFPA 855: separation distances, enclosure fire rating, gas/smoke/off-gas detection, suppression/deflagration venting (UL 9540A data), thermal management, BMS with alarms to control room, SoC limits for storage (≤ 30–50%)

PV: design per IS/IEC 60364-7-712 & IEC 62446; string/array DC isolators accessible, rapid-shutdown/firefighter isolation signage, surge/lightning protection, earthing of frames, walkways and anchor points on roofs, fragile-roof survey, edge protection; modules/inverters BIS-certified
EV charging: CEA 2023 safety provisions; RCD Type B/6 mA DC detection, emergency stop, fire detection in enclosed parking, no charging of visibly damaged vehicles
Training: electrical safe-isolation, Li-ion fire response (cooling with copious water, evacuation, do not open containers), WAH for rooftop crews
Battery waste: Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 – handover to registered recycler; damaged Li-ion quarantined in sand/metal container outdoors
steps: Lead-acid maintenance: isolate charger, ventilate, insulated tools, remove jewellery, PPE; measure cell voltages/specific gravity; top-up with distilled water; clean terminals; neutralise spills (soda); dispose electrolyte via authorised recycler.

Li-ion BESS: operate within BMS limits; alarm response plan (over-temperature → isolate string, ventilate, evacuate, fire service informed); no hot work near; quarterly inspection of connections/thermography; replace swollen/damaged modules per OEM; incident reporting as dangerous occurrence.

PV construction: WAH controls (edge protection, lifelines, nets), module handling (two persons, wind limits), DC strings left open-circuit with connectors capped until commissioning, label every DC cable/isolator, test insulation resistance before energising; AC/DC isolators lockable.

PV O&M: treat all DC as live in daylight; isolate at inverter and string level, cover modules for work on connectors if needed; thermography for hot spots; clean modules with water (no high-pressure at connectors) from safe access; vegetation control; inverter room ventilation and fire extinguishers (CO2).
Lightning: suspend rooftop work; LPS/SPD maintained; earth continuity tested annually.
EV charging: daily visual of cables/connectors; test RCDs monthly; signage; fire extinguisher (water mist/ABC) and vehicle-fire plan; no charging near flammable storage.

Fire response: Li-ion — raise alarm, isolate supply, evacuate, apply large volumes of water to cool (if trained and safe), expect re-ignition for hours, call fire service with battery chemistry info; lead-acid — isolate, ventilate, treat as hydrogen risk; PV — isolate AC/DC, do not cut live DC, inform fire service of live strings.
Records: battery logs, BMS alarms, inspection/thermography, RCD tests, PV test reports (IEC 62446), WAH permits, waste manifests.
ppe: Face shield & goggles, acid-resistant gloves/apron (lead-acid), insulated gloves/tools, arc-rated clothing for DC work above arc-flash threshold, harness for rooftops, safety boots
stop: DC string cannot be isolated for work
RCD test failed on EV charger
records: Battery maintenance logs, BMS alarm log, ventilation checks, fire-system tests, PV commissioning/inspection reports, WAH records, EV charger RCD tests, battery waste manifests

EV charging, renewable installations); IS 1651/IEEE 1635 (stationary batteries & rooms); IS 16046 (Li-ion cells); IS/IEC 60364-7-712; IS 14286 & IS 61730 (modules, QCO); IEC 62446; IS 3043; IS/IEC 62305; Battery Waste Management Rules 2022; MNRE/BIS ALMM; BOCW/OSH Code WAH duties; NBC Part 4

purpose: Prevent dust fires and explosions in plants handling combustible powders (flour, sugar, starch, spices, wood, cotton, coal, metals, pharmaceuticals, plastics, biomass).
scope: Silos, bucket elevators, conveyors, mills/grinders, dryers, dust collectors, pneumatic conveying, bagging, hoppers, bulk unloading; housekeeping of fugitive dust.
hazards: Primary explosion inside equipment propagating to buildings; secondary explosion from layered dust lifted by the first
Ignition: hot surfaces (bearings), friction sparks, static, electrical non-Ex, welding, self-heating in silos, foreign metal in mills
Dust inhalation; engulfment in silos; CO/CH4 in biomass storage
pre: Dust Hazard Analysis (NFPA 652) covering all process equipment and areas; Kst/Pmax/MIE/MIT data for each dust; revalidate every 5 years and on change
Area classification for dust (Zones 20/21/22, IEC 60079-10-2) with Ex-rated electricals (IP6X, tD); bonding and earthing of all conductive equipment and ducts

Explosion protection on equipment: venting (NFPA 68) to safe location, suppression/isolation (NFPA 69), spark detection and extinguishing on pneumatic lines, bearing temperature monitoring, magnetic separators, dust collectors outdoors or vented

Housekeeping limit: no accumulations > 0.8 mm (1/32 in) over > 5% of floor area or 90 m²; vacuum systems rated for combustible dust; no compressed-air blow-down except with equipment shut down and hot-work precautions
Hot-work and PTW system covering dust areas; silo entry = confined space with engulfment controls
steps: Daily housekeeping with Ex-rated vacuums; weekly inspection of overhead surfaces (beams, ducts, light fittings); clean dust collectors per schedule.
Operate equipment within parameters; respond to bearing-temperature, spark-detection and pressure alarms; empty collectors; keep covers closed and seals tight.
Maintain Ex equipment (IEC 60079-17 inspections), bonding straps, flexible connectors; check earth continuity quarterly.
Hot work only after shutting down dust-generating processes, cleaning within 11 m, wetting/covering, gas and dust-free verification; fire watch 1 h.
Silo/bulk storage: temperature/CO monitoring for self-heating; no entry without permit, isolation of feeds/discharge, lifeline, never stand on bridged material.
Metal powders (Al/Mg): no water-based suppression (use Class D agents), inert atmospheres, separate collectors.
Training on dust explosion basics; drills for dust-fire response (do not disturb layers; use fog, not jets).
Incident: any dust fire/deflagration is a dangerous occurrence — report within 12 h; investigate ignition source.
Review DHA on process/material change; audit annually.
ppe: FR anti-static clothing (EN 1149), conductive footwear in Zone 21, FFP2/3 or PAPR for dust, goggles, hearing protection
stop: Dust layer exceeding housekeeping limit near ignition sources
Hot work without process shutdown & cleaning
records: DHA report, area classification drawings, Ex equipment inspection register, bonding tests, housekeeping inspection logs, alarm logs, vent/suppression system maintenance, training, incident reports

t: Toxic Gas Systems – Chlorine, Ammonia & H2S
purpose: Prevent and respond to toxic gas releases from chlorination (water treatment, textiles, chemicals), ammonia refrigeration/fertilizer, and H2S in sewage/ETP/refining.
scope: Chlorine cylinders and tonners, chlorinators, bulk chlorine tanks; ammonia refrigeration plants (cold storage, dairy, pharma), ammonia storage; H2S at STP/ETP sumps, biogas, sour service.
roles: ERT with SCBA and chlorine kits
hazards: Chlorine: 1 ppm TLV, 10 ppm IDLH; dense gas pooling; valve/pigtail leaks during changeover; liquid chlorine expansion
Ammonia: 25 ppm TLV, 300 ppm IDLH, flammable 15–28%; machinery-room leaks, cold burns, oil draining, hydrostatic rupture of trapped liquid
H2S: 10 ppm TLV, 100 ppm IDLH, olfactory fatigue > 100 ppm; sudden release in sumps/manholes; biogas explosive
pre: Design: ventilated store/room with gas detection (alarm at TLV, action at 2–5× TLV), scrubber/neutralisation (chlorine: caustic; ammonia: water deluge/absorption), emergency shut-off/ESD, wind sock, access control, remote isolation; cylinders secured, with valve protection, trunnions for tonners (horizontal, valves vertical)
Emergency kits: Chlorine Institute kits A (cylinder)/B (tonner)/C (tank car); ammonia leak kit; SCBA sets (≥ 2 at entry), escape respirators for all in the area, Type B gas suits for ERT

MSIHC: threshold check (chlorine, ammonia, H2S in Schedules); site notification/safety report/on-site plan; off-site plan with District Collector; public information; mock drill annually with District Crisis Group

Procedures: changeover with two persons, leak detection (ammonia solution for chlorine; sulphur stick/litmus for ammonia), shelter-in-place rooms, evacuation routes upwind, hospital tie-up for toxic exposure (oxygen, bronchodilators)
Medical: pre-placement and periodic lung function for exposed workers
steps: Receipt: inspect cylinders/tonners (test date, valve, caps, leaks); store cool, shaded, segregated from flammables/oxidisers; full/empty marked; never hydrostatically fill lines (ammonia: no liquid traps without relief).
Connection/changeover: two trained persons with escape respirators; new gaskets/pigtails; open valve slowly ≤ 1 turn; leak test immediately; keep valve key on stem; close empties and cap.
Operation: continuous detection and ventilation; weekly check of alarms/scrubber; monthly simulated leak drill; maintain relief valves (ammonia 5-yearly replacement typical), vent to safe height.

Minor leak: approach upwind with SCBA, isolate at source, apply kit, neutralise, ventilate; never spray water on a chlorine cylinder leak (increases corrosion/evaporation) — for liquid chlorine turn cylinder so leak is in gas phase; ammonia: water fog to knock down vapour (not on liquid pool), avoid runoff to drains.

Major release: sound toxic-gas alarm, evacuate crosswind/upwind, account for persons, shelter-in-place for non-ERT, notify fire service/police/District authorities and neighbours, medical triage, MSIHC 48-h report (and dangerous-occurrence notice 12 h).
H2S areas: treat sumps/manholes/digesters as permit-required confined spaces; continuous personal monitors; ventilation; never work alone; biogas lines with flame arresters and LEL monitoring.
Maintenance: isolation and purging (ammonia: pump-down, nitrogen purge; chlorine: evacuate with air/N2), PTW, gas testing, LOTO; hot work only after purge and test.
Training: all site personnel in alarm response and escape-respirator use; ERT quarterly drills; records; review after any leak.
ppe: Escape respirator (all), SCBA and Type B gas suit (ERT), chemical goggles/face shield, gloves (neoprene/butyl for ammonia; PVC for chlorine), cold-protective gloves for ammonia, personal gas monitors
stop: Two trained persons not available for changeover
Emergency kit or SCBA out of service
records: Cylinder register, changeover logs, leak-test records, detector calibration/alarm tests, scrubber checks, drill reports, MSIHC documents, medical surveillance, incident reports

purpose: Prevent collapse, inrush, hazardous atmospheres, fire, hoisting incidents and decompression illness in underground construction.
scope: TBM/EPB tunnels, NATM/drill-and-blast, cut-and-cover, shafts, cross-passages, micro-tunnelling, pipe jacking, compressed-air interventions; metro, water, road and utility tunnels.
roles: Compressed-air medical lock attendant & medical adviser
hazards: Face/crown collapse, inrush of water/mud, settlement affecting surface structures
O2 deficiency, methane/CO/H2S/radon, diesel fumes; fire in confined tunnel; explosives (D&B)
Shaft hoisting failures, falling objects, falls at shaft edge; TBM rotating parts, segment erector crush, conveyor
Compressed-air work: decompression illness, barotrauma, O2 toxicity, fire risk in hyperbaric atmosphere
Flooding from storm; power failure; long escape distances
pre: Geotechnical investigation and ground-support design; monitoring (convergence, settlement, piezometers) with trigger levels; probe drilling ahead where water/gas risk
Ventilation design (≥ 6 m³/min per person; velocity ≥ 0.3 m/s – OSHA 200 cfm/30 fpm), continuous multi-gas monitoring at face/invert, alarms, Ex equipment in gassy ground
Access control: tally/check-in system (every person tagged), communication (leaky feeder/radio/telephone), lighting, refuge chambers with air/water/comms, self-rescuers for all, escape routes marked
Shaft: hoist/cage certified (test after installation and 6-monthly – verify rules), banksman at top and bottom, gates interlocked, falling-object protection, edge protection
Fire: no accumulation of combustibles, fire-rated hydraulic oils, extinguishers/foam at TBM, emergency stop of ventilation only by controller, hot-work permits

Compressed air: medical examinations, medical lock with attendant, decompression tables per regulations, pressure records, emergency medical cover (hyperbaric physician), no smoking/flame, fire-resistant materials in chamber
Emergency plan agreed with fire service (tunnel rescue), flood response (pump capacity, bulkheads), blasting procedures (if D&B)
steps: Daily shift briefing: ground conditions, monitoring results, gas readings, planned activities; tally in/out.
Ground support installed per design without delay; inspect face/crown each shift; stop and support on any instability; dewatering maintained.

Gas: continuous readings logged; action levels (CH4 ≥ 0.25–1% depending on regime: increase ventilation / withdraw; CO ≥ 25 ppm; O2 < 19.5%) with evacuation above limits; no entry after ventilation outage until re-tested.
TBM: segment erection under guarded zone; exclusion from cutter-head area; interventions in the chamber under PTW (atmospheric or hyperbaric); conveyor guards; grout/foam chemicals with SDS/PPE.
Shaft operations: banksman controls all hoisting; loads secured in cage; no riding with loads unless designed; drop zone cleared; hoist inspection daily.
Vehicles/locos: speed limits, lighting, refuge niches, pedestrian walkways, diesel exhaust control (DPF) and CO monitoring.
Compressed air: pressurisation/decompression per tables with attendant; max working pressure and durations; medical lock on standby; worker identification cards (hyperbaric) for 24 h after work.

Emergency: alarm, evacuation to refuge/portal, self-rescuers, head-count against tally, rescue team entry only with BA and plan; flood – withdraw and close bulkheads; fire – isolate power, suppress if safe.
Surface: settlement monitoring, utility protection, public safety at shafts (fencing, lighting, noise/vibration limits).
Records: monitoring, gas logs, tally, hoist inspection, compressed-air logs, medical records, drills.
ppe: Helmet with lamp, hi-vis, boots, self-rescuer, gas monitor, hearing protection, gloves; respirator for dust; harness at shafts
stop: Gas above action level or ventilation failure
Flooding or power failure without backup
records: Ground monitoring, shift reports, gas logs, tally system records, hoist certificates/inspections, PTWs, compressed-air logs & medicals, drills, incident reports

Client manuals: BMRCL/CMRL safety, health & environment manuals; IS 4081, IS 3764

purpose: Prevent rig overturn, entanglement in augers/rotaries, falls into open bores, struck-by from cages and tremie pipes, and vibration/noise harm.
scope: Bored cast-in-situ piles (rotary/DMC), CFA, driven precast/steel piles, sheet piles, diaphragm walls, micro-piles, ground anchors; associated rebar cage fabrication and concreting.
hazards: Rig overturn on soft/uneven platform; slewing with mast raised; tracking near excavations
Entanglement with rotating auger/kelly; auger cleaning by hand; falling spoil from auger
Open bores (fall/drowning), collapse of bore, bentonite slurry handling, casing extraction forces
Rebar cage instability/collapse during lifting; tremie pipe handling; concrete pump boom
Noise/vibration to workers and neighbours; overhead/underground services; diesel/hydraulic fire
pre: Working platform designed (bearing/mat) with certificate; drainage; inspected daily and after rain; edge distances from excavations/slopes defined

Rig: manufacturer manual, daily checks, mast raising procedure, wind limits, anti-entanglement (no loose clothing), auger cleaner device, emergency stops; rig operator trained (OEM/recognised); tracking plan with banksman
Service crane and lifting plans for cages/casings; cages designed for lifting (stiffeners, lifting points), tag lines; exclusion zones
Bore protection: casing/collar above ground, covers for open bores, barriers, lighting; bentonite plant bunded; slurry disposal under waste rules
Utility survey and overhead-line clearance; permit-to-dig; vibration/noise monitoring near sensitive receptors; blasting-like PPV limits for driven piles
steps: Set up rig on certified platform; level; check ground under tracks; mast raised only per manual with exclusion zone; secure kelly/auger.
Drilling: nobody within rig swing/auger zone; banksman communicates with operator; auger spoil removed mechanically; never clean auger by hand while rotating; stop rotation before approach.
Open bores covered/ barricaded immediately; casings extended above ground; no stepping over bores.
Rebar cage: fabricated on level beds; lifted with designed points and spreader; guided with tag lines; no persons under; secured in bore before release; splices from platform with edge protection.
Concreting: tremie pipe handling with crane/hoist, pipe lengths secured; concrete pump boom clearances; overflow/slurry displacement managed; PPE for cement.
Driven piles: hammer guards, exclusion for flying debris, hearing protection, vibration monitoring; sheet-pile handling with clamps and tag lines; trench support where excavated.
Bentonite/polymer: SDS, dust control on mixing, bunds, de-sanding, disposal manifests; slip hazards cleaned.
Pile cutting/trimming: silica dust control (wet), hydraulic croppers preferred; vibration limits.
Daily platform inspection, rig checks, lifting-gear checks recorded; incidents and near-misses reviewed; neighbours' complaints logged.
ppe: Helmet, hi-vis, boots, gloves, eye protection, hearing protection, FFP2/3 for cutting, harness at open excavations
stop: Person inside auger/kelly zone while rotating
Cage lifting without plan or inadequate lifting points
records: Working platform certificate & daily checks, rig inspections, operator competence, lifting plans, bore log/cover checks, waste manifests, vibration/noise logs, incidents

india: BOCW Central Rules 1998 & KA/TN BOCW Rules (excavation, lifting appliances, electrical); IS 2911 (pile foundations – construction), IS 3764, IS 13367; CEA clearances; Noise Rules 2000; HOWM (bentonite sludge)
ka: Karnataka BOCW Rules 2006; KSPCB bentonite/slurry disposal; BBMP
tn: TN BOCW Rules 2006; TNPCB; CMDA conditions
osha: 1926 Subpart CC (cranes; 1926.1400 applies to pile-driving cranes), 1926.603 (pile driving equipment), 1926.651, 1926.251
intl: BS EN 16228 series; FPS/BDA guidance (UK) on working platforms, auger cleaning, cage lifting; HSE 'Piling' guidance; ILO

purpose: Prevent premature detonation, flyrock, ground-vibration damage, misfire incidents and theft/loss of explosives.
scope: Rock excavation for foundations, roads, tunnels, quarries supplying aggregates; controlled blasting near structures; explosives storage and transport.
roles: Site safety officer; liaison with police/DM
hazards: Flyrock beyond exclusion zone; ground vibration/airblast damaging structures; noise
Misfires and unexploded charges; premature initiation (stray current, lightning, RF for electric detonators)
Theft/diversion of explosives; transport incidents; unauthorised storage
Dust and toxic fumes (NOx) after blast
pre: Licences: magazine (LE-3/LE-5) at approved distance, possession/use licence, transport (explosives van, licensed driver), shot-firer certificate; police/District Magistrate intimation and local conditions (timings, siren)

Blasting plan: survey of structures within influence zone, PPV limits per DGMS circular (e.g., 5–15 mm/s domestic depending on frequency), charge per delay calculated, burden/spacing/stemming design, controlled blasting (line drilling, pre-splitting, blasting mats) near structures, exclusion radius (typically 300–500 m) with sentries, shelters for crew
Monitoring: seismograph at nearest structure for every blast near habitation; pre-blast structural condition survey with photographs; community notice
Storage: magazine construction/ventilation/lightning protection per rules; detonators separate from explosives; registers (receipt/issue/return daily); CCTV/guards
Procedures: electric/non-electric (NONEL) initiation choice considering stray current/RF; lightning – suspend; misfire procedure; fume clearance time
steps: Drill pattern per plan; log hole depths; clear water/debris; no smoking/flames in the area; keep explosives in day-boxes only as needed.
Charge holes by shot-firer: primers prepared at hole, detonator leads shunted (electric), stemming with inert material; account for every detonator/cartridge against issue.

Clear the exclusion zone: sentries at all approaches with radios, warning signs, siren sequence (e.g., 3 long = clear, 1 long = fire, 2 short = all clear); verify by radio check that all sentries report clear; crew in shelter.
Fire from safe position/shelter; count detonations; wait the prescribed interval before approach (electric ≥ 5–30 min; safety fuse ≥ 30–60 min per rules; DGMS: no approach until fumes clear).
Post-blast: shot-firer inspects alone first for misfires/butts; if misfire, mark, keep area closed, re-fire or sleep per procedure (never drill into a misfired hole); flush/wash out with water; log.
Return unused explosives to magazine same day; reconcile registers; report discrepancies to PESO/police immediately.
Record seismograph readings; compare with limits; stop and redesign if exceeded; handle complaints via pre-blast survey records.
Transport: approved explosives van, no mixed load with detonators, escort where required, route plan, no stops in populated areas.
Emergency: lightning – evacuate charging area; fire near magazine – evacuate 500 m+, call fire service with information; accident – PESO forthwith.
ppe: Helmet, boots, hi-vis, hearing protection, eye protection, dust mask; no synthetic clothing when handling detonators (static)
stop: Seismograph reading above limit at structures
records: Licences, magazine registers, blasting plans, daily shot records, seismograph records, pre-blast surveys, misfire logs, police/DM intimations, transport logs

india: Explosives Act 1884; Explosives Rules 2008 (licensing, magazines, transport, shot-firer, accident notice); Ammonium Nitrate Rules 2012; IS 4081; DGMS Technical Circular 7/1997 (vibration limits); Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961/ Mines Rules for quarries; BOCW Central Rules (explosives chapter); OSH Code s.11 (dangerous occurrence)
ka: Karnataka Minor Mineral Concession Rules 1994 (quarries); DM/police permissions; Karnataka BOCW Rules
tn: TN Minor Mineral Concession Rules 1959 (quarries); DM/police; TN BOCW Rules
osha: 1926 Subpart U (1926.900–914) blasting and use of explosives; MSHA 30 CFR 56/57 (quarries)
intl: UK Explosives Regulations 2014; BS 5607 (safe use of explosives in construction); ISEE Blasters' Handbook; AS 2187.2

t: Abrasive Blasting, Surface Preparation & Spray Painting / Coatings
purpose: Prevent silicosis/lung disease, isocyanate asthma, solvent fires, hearing loss, eye injuries and falls in blasting and painting operations.
scope: Grit/shot/garnet blasting of steel, tanks, bridges; water-jetting; wire brushing; spray painting (airless/air-assisted), 2-pack polyurethane/epoxy coatings, lead-paint removal; blast rooms and open-site work.
hazards: Silica from sand blasting (prohibited/strictly controlled under state rules – use garnet/steel grit/copper slag with low free silica), nuisance dust, lead/chromate from old paints
Isocyanates (2K PU) – occupational asthma, sensitisation; solvents – fire/explosion, CNS effects; epoxy dermatitis
Breathing-air contamination (CO, oil) from compressors; hose rupture; dead-man valve failure; high-pressure water injection
Noise > 100 dB(A); falls from scaffolds/ropes; confined-space in tanks; static ignition of solvent mists
pre: Substitute: no silica sand; vacuum/wet blasting or water-jetting where feasible; low-VOC/water-based coatings; lead/chromate survey before stripping old paint

Blasting: enclosed blast room or screens/tenting with ventilation and dust collector; CE/EN 14594 supplied-air blast helmet with breathing-air quality tested (CO < 10 ppm, oil, particulates – EN 12021), CO alarm on air supply, dead-man control on nozzle, hose couplings with safety pins/whip-checks, pressure vessel certified (SMPV/Factories Rules)

Painting: spray booths with LEV and filters; Zone 1/2 classification with Ex equipment; earthing/bonding of airless units; solvent storage in cabinets; RPE for isocyanates (air-fed hood/visor or full-face with A2P3 only for short tasks), skin protection; health surveillance (spirometry baseline/annual, isocyanate monitoring)
Confined-space entry procedure for tank interiors (LEL monitoring, forced ventilation, Ex lighting); hot-work exclusion zone (no welding within 15 m of spraying); fire watch and extinguishers
WAH controls for scaffolds/rope access (IRATA)
steps: Prepare area: barricade and signage; cover sensitive equipment; collect spent abrasive (hazardous if lead/chromate) in bins; protect drains.
Blasting: pre-use checks of pot, hoses, couplings, dead-man, helmet airline; attendant monitors compressor/CO alarm; blaster never points nozzle at persons; rest breaks; daily hose inspection.
Clean-up with vacuum (HEPA) — no dry sweeping or compressed air; dispose abrasive per waste rules (TSDF if contaminated).
Mixing paints: in ventilated area, SDS, correct ratios, labelled containers, static bonding, no ignition sources; keep quantities ≤ shift need.

Spraying: Ex equipment and lighting, ventilation running before/during/after; airless gun with trigger lock; never clear tip with finger; injection injury = emergency (hospital even if small wound); overspray control; mist LEL monitoring in enclosed spaces.

Isocyanates: air-fed RPE, cover all skin, decontaminate before breaks, no eating in area, monitor exposure, remove sensitised workers; keep away other trades until cured (typically 30 min after spraying, ventilated).
Drying/curing: ventilation continues; no hot work until solvent vapours clear (test LEL).
Waste: empty tins, rags, thinners = hazardous waste; manifest; no burning.
Records: breathing-air tests, exposure monitoring, health surveillance, equipment inspections, permits.
ppe: Blast helmet with supplied air (EN 14594/NIOSH type CE), leather/canvas blast suit, gloves, hearing protection; painters – air-fed hood or A2P3 full-face, chemical gloves (nitrile/butyl), coveralls (Type 5/6), goggles, safety boots; anti-static clothing in Zone 1
stop: Breathing-air CO alarm or supply failure
Hot work within exclusion zone of spraying
records: Abrasive SDS/free-silica certificate, breathing-air quality tests, equipment checks, exposure monitoring, health surveillance, permits (confined space/hot work), waste manifests

II PELs (silica, lead, solvents, isocyanates), s.37 (flammable vapour); OSH Code s.6, s.12 (silicosis, asthma); Petroleum Rules (solvents Class A/B); IS/IEC 60079; HOWM (spent abrasive, paint waste); IS 15656

tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 Rule 95 (sand-blasting, spraying, lead schedules); TNPCB
osha: 1910.94 ventilation (abrasive blasting, spray finishing), 1910.107 spray finishing, 1910.1053/1926.1153 silica, 1926.62 lead, 1910.134 respirators (Grade D breathing air), 1926.57; NFPA 33, 34
intl: UK COSHH; HSE guidance on isocyanate paint spraying (motor vehicle repair/industrial); EN 12021 breathing air; EN 14594; ISO 8501 (surface prep); ATEX

t: Working Over or Near Water & Marine/Jetty Works
purpose: Prevent drowning, falls into water, vessel/barge incidents and hypothermia during bridge, jetty, intake, outfall, dam and coastal works.
scope: Piers and bridges over rivers/sea, jetties, breakwaters, intake/outfall pipelines, dredging support, work from barges/pontoons, cofferdams, river diversion, monsoon river sites.
roles: Safety officer; dive supervisor where diving
hazards: Falls into fast/tidal water; entrapment under pontoons; cold water/hypothermia; strong currents and floods
Barge instability during crane lifts; mooring failures; man overboard; collisions
Cofferdam collapse/inundation; sudden dam/river releases; monsoon flash floods
Water-borne disease; crocodiles/sea snakes/jellyfish in some locations
pre: Edge protection/nets over water preferred; where not feasible, lifejackets (≥ 150 N, auto-inflating, with light/whistle) worn by all within 2 m of edge or on vessels; harness only where it cannot drag worker under water (restraint)

Rescue: manned rescue boat (engine running) with trained crew during work over water, lifebuoys with 30 m line at ≤ 50 m intervals, throw bags, ladders/scramble nets down to water, communication; man-overboard drill monthly

Vessels: certified (survey), stability calculations for crane/plant on barge, load limits, moorings designed for tide/current, navigation lights, port/harbour permissions, weather (IMD) monitoring with stop criteria
Cofferdams: design for flood level with freeboard, pumps on standby, evacuation alarm and route, river release schedule from dam authority
Medical: swimming ability recorded; hypothermia response; tetanus; leptospirosis/water-borne disease precautions
steps: Daily briefing: tide/current/weather, vessel assignments, rescue arrangements, emergency signals.
Access via gangways with handrails and nets; no jumping between vessels; boarding only when secured.
Work from barges: keep plant within marked positions; crane lifts within afloat chart (reduced capacity) and with stability check; no lifts in swell beyond limits; tag lines.
Lifejacket check each shift (gas cylinder, indicator); PPE compatible with buoyancy; helmets with chin straps.
Rescue boat positioned downstream/down-current of work; crew in position; radio checks hourly.
Night work only with lighting over water and additional rescue cover.
Cofferdam/river works: monitor water level; alarms; evacuate at trigger level; after heavy rain upstream, suspend work.
Diving (if any): only under diving contractor's procedures (IMCA/DG Shipping), dive supervisor, standby diver, medical, decompression; isolation of intakes/pumps (LOTO) before diving.
Emergency: man overboard — throw buoy, keep sight, boat rescue, hypothermia treatment; vessel incident — port authority/coast guard (1554) informed.
ppe: Lifejacket/PFD, helmet with chin strap, non-slip boots, gloves, hi-vis, harness/restraint where specified, sun/thermal protection
stop: Barge stability not verified for the lift
records: Rescue arrangements and drills, vessel certificates/stability, mooring inspections, lifejacket checks, weather logs, permits, incident reports

india: IS 13416 Pt 5 (prevention of drowning); BOCW Central Rules 1998 (work near water); KA/TN BOCW Rules; Dock Workers Regulations 1990 (ports, via OSH Code); Merchant Shipping Act & DG Shipping/IRS rules for vessels; Port Trust/Maritime Board rules; CRZ Notification 2019; OSH Code s.6
ka: New Mangalore Port/ Karnataka Maritime Board; Karnataka BOCW Rules; KSDMA flood alerts (Kaveri, coastal)
tn: Chennai/Ennore/Kamarajar/VOC Port rules; TN Maritime Board; TNSDMA cyclone alerts; TN BOCW Rules

intl: UK HSE 'Working over or near water'; EN ISO 12402 PFDs; IMCA diving; ILO C152

purpose: Prevent workers and public being struck by traffic/plant, bitumen burns, fire and fume exposure during road construction and resurfacing.
scope: Highway/urban road works, paving, milling, chip sealing, hot-mix plant operation, bitumen tanker transfer, kerb/drain works, lane closures, night works.
hazards: Vehicles entering work zone; plant reversing; night visibility; speeding public traffic
Hot bitumen (150–180 °C) burns from splash, hose failure, tanker overflow; steam explosion if water enters hot bitumen; fire of cutback/kerosene; bitumen fumes (PAHs), H2S in tankers
HMP: burner flame-out/explosion, hot aggregate, dryer drum, noise, dust, conveyor nip points, bag-house fire
Manual handling of kerbs, heat stress, utility strikes, trench collapse for drains
pre: Traffic management plan per IRC:SP:55 with police approval: advance warning signs, taper/transition with cones/barriers, buffer zone, work zone, termination; speed limits; night lighting and retro-reflective signage; flaggers with paddles/radios; diversion plan
Plant: reversing alarms/cameras, beacons, banksman; paver/roller operators trained; refuelling procedure

Bitumen: storage/heating tanks with temperature control and high-level alarms, no water contact, transfer by earthed hoses with dry couplings, PPE and burn first-aid (cool water 20 min; do not remove bitumen from skin; burns centre tie-up), emulsion preferred over cutback; kerosene/cutback as Class B petroleum (PESO licence if > 2,500 L)

HMP: SPCB consent and siting distance (verify state norm, typically ≥ 500 m from habitation), stack/bag-house maintenance, burner interlocks, dust suppression, noise enclosures, fire extinguishers, LOTO for maintenance
Heat stress and hydration plan; utility survey for drain/kerb excavation
steps: Install traffic controls before starting; inspect at shift start, after any change and at night; maintain sign faces clean and reflective.
Keep workers facing traffic where possible; marshals control plant movements; no work between moving plant and barrier without lookout.
Paving: exclusion around paver/roller; no riding on screed; hot mix handled with gloves/boots; keep off fresh mat edges near traffic.

Bitumen transfer: check tanker temperature (not above flash point minus margin; no foaming), earth tanker, connect dry-break couplings, operator at valve, nobody near outlet; never open a tanker hatch that may contain water; store sprayer bars safely.
HMP operation: start-up sequence (purge, ignition), monitor burner, bag-house temperatures, aggregate moisture; conveyor guards; housekeeping of fines; stop on flame-out and purge before re-ignition.
Milling/cutting: dust control (water), silica RPE, hearing protection, debris control.
Night works: full lighting, class 3 hi-vis, fatigue breaks, extra marshals; coordinate with police.
Removal of traffic controls in reverse order; clean road; report incidents and near-misses (public vehicle intrusions).
Emergency: bitumen burn protocol; vehicle intrusion — stop work, raise alarm; fire at HMP — isolate fuel, extinguish, call 101.
ppe: Class 2/3 hi-vis, helmet, safety boots (heat-resistant soles near bitumen), gloves (heat/cut), face shield + goggles for bitumen handling, long sleeves, hearing protection, FFP2 for dust
stop: Water contamination risk at hot bitumen
Reversing without banksman in work zone
records: Traffic management plan & police permission, daily sign inspections, plant checks, bitumen temperature logs, HMP consent & stack results, burn-incident log, training of flaggers

india: IRC:SP:55; IRC:SP:98 / MoRTH Specifications; MV Act 1988; BOCW rules; Petroleum Rules 2002 (cutbacks/kerosene); Air Act/SPCB HMP consent; Noise Rules; IS 3764 (drain excavation); OSH Code s.6
ka: KSPCB HMP conditions; Bengaluru traffic police road-cutting/closure permits; Karnataka BOCW Rules
tn: TNPCB HMP conditions; Chennai traffic police permits; TN BOCW Rules; TN Highways Dept specifications
osha: 1926 Subpart G (signs/signals/barricades), 1926.201 (flaggers), MUTCD Part 6 (temporary traffic control); 1926.600–602; 1910.106
intl: UK Safety at Street Works and Road Works Code (Red Book); Eurobitume/HSE 'Safe handling of bitumen'; ILO

purpose: Protect laboratory staff from chemical, biological, physical and fire hazards in plant QC, R&D and testing labs.
scope: Analytical/QC labs in chemical, pharma, food, cement, steel and construction-material testing; microbiology labs (BSL-1/2); pilot plants by analogy.
hazards: Chemical exposure (solvents, acids, HF, cyanides, carcinogens), splashes to eyes, peroxide-formers, incompatible storage
Fire from solvents/heating mantles; pressure/vacuum glassware implosion; compressed gases; cryogenics (asphyxiation, cold burns)
Biological agents, sharps, aerosols; autoclave burns
Ergonomics (pipetting), electrical, heavy equipment (presses, ovens, muffle furnaces in material-testing labs)
pre: Chemical hygiene plan; SDS library; chemical inventory with max quantities; segregated storage (acids/bases/oxidisers/flammables); flammables ≤ 10 L on bench, cabinets for more; peroxide-former dating/testing
Fume hoods (face velocity 0.4–0.5 m/s, annual test), biosafety cabinets (annual certification), LEV at instruments; eyewash and safety shower within 10 s, tested weekly
Gas cylinders secured, regulators matched, leak checks; cryogen handling PPE and O2 monitors in storage rooms
Waste: segregated solvent/halogenated/aqueous/sharps/bio streams, labelled, manifested (HW/BMW rules); autoclave validation
Training (incl. HF first aid – calcium gluconate gel), emergency procedures, lab access control, no lone working with hazardous procedures
steps: Plan experiments/tests with risk assessment; use smallest quantities; prefer closed systems.
Wear lab coat, goggles, gloves per SDS; no food/drink; tie hair; closed shoes; wash hands.
Work in hood with sash low; keep hood uncluttered; never store chemicals in hood.
Heating: mantles/water baths over open flames; no unattended heating; use pressure-rated vessels; shield vacuum glassware.
Label all containers (name, hazard, date, owner); date peroxide-formers (ethers) and discard per policy.
Spills: small – trained staff with kit; large/toxic – evacuate, ventilate, call ERT; mercury spills with specific kit.
Biological: BSL-2 practices, biosafety cabinet for aerosols, autoclave waste, disinfect surfaces, sharps containers, immunisations/medical surveillance.
Material-testing labs: guard presses/compression machines, hot-sample handling from ovens/furnaces with tongs/gloves, silica dust from grinding (LEV), noise.
Housekeeping, weekly safety inspection, chemical inventory review quarterly, equipment electrical safety (PAT), emergency drills.
ppe: Lab coat (FR for flammable work), chemical splash goggles, face shield for acids/HF, nitrile/neoprene gloves, cryogenic gloves/face shield, respirator for specific tasks, closed-toe shoes
records: Chemical inventory, SDS register, hood/BSC tests, eyewash tests, waste manifests, training, incident/near-miss, medical surveillance (bio)

tn: DISH TN; TNPCB; TN BMW authorisation

t: Biological Hazards, Vector Control, Water Hygiene & Pandemic Readiness
purpose: Prevent infectious disease outbreaks (vector-, water- and air-borne), animal bites and bloodborne exposures at sites, factories and labour camps.
scope: Construction camps and canteens, factory OHCs, cooling towers/water systems, STP/ETP operators, waste handlers, security/first-aiders; pandemic/epidemic response.
hazards: Dengue/malaria/chikungunya (stagnant water), leptospirosis (flood water), typhoid/cholera/hepatitis A (water/food), TB/influenza/COVID-type outbreaks in dense camps
Snake/scorpion/dog bites (rabies), tetanus from injuries
Bloodborne pathogens for first-aiders, sharps in waste, legionella from cooling towers/showers, H2S/biological at STPs
pre: Camp/site standards: potable water (IS 10500; tested monthly; chlorination), food safety (FSSAI-registered canteens, hygiene training), toilets/bathing, drainage, waste collection, bedding spacing/ventilation, isolation room
Vector control plan: weekly source reduction (no stagnant water in tyres, drums, excavations), larvicide, fogging in season, nets/repellents, ULB coordination; monsoon campaign

Medical: pre-employment screening, vaccinations as advised (tetanus, hepatitis B for first-aiders/waste handlers, typhoid), antivenom/rabies PEP availability mapped to hospitals, first-aid kits with bite protocol
Water systems: legionella risk assessment of cooling towers/hot water (temperature control, biocide dosing, cleaning quarterly/6-monthly, sampling), drift eliminators, records

Outbreak plan: case definition, reporting to District Health Officer (notifiable diseases), isolation, contact tracing, PPE stocks (masks, gloves, sanitiser), remote-work/shift segregation, communication in local languages
steps: Daily camp inspection: water, toilets, waste, drainage; weekly larval survey; act on findings within 24 h.
Food: canteen hygiene audit monthly; food handlers' medical certificates; safe storage temperatures.

Bites: snake — immobilise limb, no cutting/sucking/tourniquet, hospital with antivenom within 1 h; dog/animal — wash wound 15 min with soap, rabies PEP; scorpion — hospital (prazosin where indicated); record and remove attractants (rodents, debris piles).
Injuries: tetanus prophylaxis per vaccination status; first-aiders use gloves, sharps containers, disinfect; post-exposure protocol for needle-stick (OHC/hospital).
STP/ETP: PPE (gloves, boots, goggles), H2S monitoring, hand hygiene, vaccination (hepatitis), confined-space procedure for sumps.

Cooling towers: monthly inspection, biocide/scale control, cleaning and disinfection per schedule, Legionella sampling where risk assessment requires; shut down and clean after any positive result; shower heads descaled.
Respiratory outbreaks: screening at gate, masks, ventilation, isolation, report cluster to health authority, stagger shifts; follow MoHFW/State advisories.
Records: water tests, vector control log, medical cases/outbreak reports, vaccination, cooling-tower maintenance.
ppe: Gloves, masks (as per risk), boots, goggles for waste/STP; repellents/nets for camps
stop: Antivenom/rabies PEP access not confirmed for remote site
Cooling tower positive Legionella without action
records: Water quality tests, vector control & larval survey logs, canteen audits, vaccination records, bite/injury register, outbreak reports to health authority, cooling-tower logs

t: Site Security, Workplace Violence & Public Safety
purpose: Protect people, assets and the public from unauthorised access, theft, violence, harassment, civil disturbance and threats, and ensure security measures never compromise emergency egress.
scope: Perimeter and access control, visitor/contractor management, materials control, CCTV, guarding, cash/explosives/fuel/chemical security, hoardings and public walkways, labour unrest, harassment (POSH), threats and bomb calls.
hazards: Theft of scaffold/formwork components (collapse risk), cable theft (electrical hazards), fuel/explosives diversion
Unauthorised entry into hazardous areas; trespass by children into excavations/water bodies
Violence/harassment; crowd events during unrest; vehicle ramming at gates
Security measures that lock fire exits or block emergency access
pre: Risk-based security plan; licensed guards with verified antecedents; shift rosters; training in emergency response and first aid
Access control: ID cards/biometric, visitor register and escorts, vehicle gate passes, material in/out registers, key control; hazardous stores (explosives, chemicals, fuel) with locks/CCTV/logs
Perimeter: fencing/hoarding ≥ 2 m, lighting, CCTV with 30-day retention, signage; public walkways with overhead protection where work above; excavations fenced at night
Policies: POSH (ICC constituted, displayed), anti-violence, grievance redressal (IR Code committees), drug/alcohol, weapons prohibition; threat/bomb-call procedure; media policy
Coordination with police (beat officer contacts), fire service; emergency egress must never be locked — security checks exits daily
steps: Gate: verify ID/induction before entry; log visitors; issue PPE; vehicles inspected; hazardous materials checked against manifests.
Patrols: perimeter and hazardous stores every shift; night checks of cranes/hoists isolation, fuel bunds, excavation fencing; report defects.
Public safety: maintain hoardings, covered walkways, debris nets; no material stored on public footpath; traffic marshals at site exits; night lighting.

Incidents: theft/trespass — secure, record, report to police; violence/harassment — immediate safety, medical aid, report via ICC/HR, no retaliation; unrest — de-escalate, protect lives, inform police, safe shutdown of plant (process isolation) if needed.
Threats/bomb calls: record details, inform site head/police, evacuate per plan without panic, do not touch suspicious objects.
Workplace violence prevention: training for supervisors, lone-worker protection, cash handling controls, exit interviews for grievances.
Drills: security breach and threat scenarios annually with emergency plan.
Audit quarterly: access logs, CCTV function, guard training, exit integrity; review after incidents.
ppe: Guards: hi-vis, helmet/boots where on site, torches, radios
records: Security plan, guard licences, access/visitor logs, material registers, CCTV logs, incident reports (police FIR copies), ICC records, drills, audits

purpose: Use drones safely and lawfully for progress surveys, structural/roof/stack/flare inspections and confined-area reconnaissance, reducing work at height and confined-space entry.
scope: Nano/micro/small drones for photogrammetry, thermal inspection of roofs/solar/substations, chimney/flare inspection, tank internal inspection (caged drones), site security.
roles: Remote pilot (DGCA Remote Pilot Certificate for applicable classes)
hazards: Drone strike on persons/plant/lines; loss of control/fly-away; Li-Po battery fire; propeller injuries
Flying in restricted zones (airport, defence) – legal violations; privacy; distraction of crane operators
pre: DGCA compliance: type-certified drone with UIN; remote pilot certificate; Digital Sky zone check (green zone or permission); ≤ 120 m AGL; VLOS; insurance; no flight over crowds or near cranes in operation without coordination

Site SOP: flight plan, exclusion of persons under flight path, coordination with crane/lifting operations (no simultaneous), weather limits (wind, rain), battery management (fire-safe charging bags/cabinet), emergency landing areas
Industrial sites: hazardous-area check (no non-Ex drones in Zone 1/2 during operation), permits from plant control room, EMI near substations
steps: Pre-flight: zone check, NOTAM/airspace, weather, battery/propeller/firmware check, geofence set, return-to-home altitude above obstacles.
Brief site: announce flight, cordon take-off/landing area, spotter assigned, crane operators informed (stop lifts in overlap).
Fly within VLOS; avoid people, lines and structures by safe margins; abort on control/signal loss warnings.
Internal tank/duct inspections: caged drone, confined-space hazards still apply to any human entry; atmosphere test for ignition risk if flammable vapours.
Post-flight: logs, battery storage at 40–60% charge, data secured (privacy), defects reported; incidents/near-misses reported (and to DGCA where required).
Maintenance per OEM; propeller replacement; annual review of SOP and certificates.
ppe: Standard; safety glasses for pilots near take-off; gloves for battery handling
stop: Wind above limit, rain, low visibility
Persons under flight path cannot be cleared
records: Pilot certificates, UIN, flight logs, zone permissions, battery logs, incident reports

t: Carbon Accounting – GHG Inventory (Scope 1/2/3), CCTS Compliance & Verification
purpose: Produce an auditable organisational GHG inventory aligned with GHG Protocol/ISO 14064-1, meet CCTS obligations where the site is an obligated entity, and supply CBAM data to EU customers.
scope: All sites: stationary combustion (boilers, furnaces, DG sets, kilns), mobile combustion (fleet, site plant), process emissions (cement calcination, steel, chemicals), fugitive (refrigerants, SF6, methane), purchased electricity/steam, and Scope 3 categories material to the business (purchased goods, fuel & energy, upstream transport, waste, business travel, commuting, use of sold products).
roles: Sustainability/energy manager (BEE-certified energy manager where designated consumer)
Site data owners (utilities, stores, fleet, maintenance)
Internal auditor; Accredited Carbon Verification Agency (ACVA) / assurance provider
hazards: Data gaps and double counting; wrong emission factors; unverifiable claims (greenwashing liability under SEBI/ASCI/EU rules)
Missing CCTS deadlines → CCC purchase/penalty; CBAM default-value mark-ups
pre: Boundary: operational control; list of sites and sources; base year (CCTS: FY2023-24); materiality thresholds

Emission factors: IPCC 2006 for fuels (diesel ≈ 2.68 kg CO2/L, petrol ≈ 2.3, LPG ≈ 3.0 kg/kg, natural gas ≈ 1.9 kg/SCM, furnace oil ≈ 3.1 kg/kg, Indian non-coking coal ≈ 1.6–1.9 t CO2/t by grade), CEA grid factor (v20: 0.727 tCO2/MWh FY2023-24), GWPs (IPCC AR5/AR6 as required by the scheme), process factors (e.g. clinker 0.52 tCO2/t); BEE-specified factors override for CCTS
Data systems: metered fuel/electricity, stores issue records, refrigerant purchase/leak logs, production data; monthly data close; QA/QC checks
CCTS (obligated entities): monitoring plan submitted/approved by BEE; monthly monitoring; registry account (Grid-India); ACVA appointed; GEI target known
CBAM (exporters): product–CN code mapping; installation-level direct/indirect emissions; precursor data; verifier; CBAM registry access via EU customer
steps: Collect monthly activity data by source; reconcile with finance (fuel invoices, electricity bills) and production.

Calculate Scope 1 by source (fuel × NCV × EF; process; fugitive = purchases − returns ± inventory change × GWP); Scope 2 location-based (kWh × grid factor) and market-based (contracts/RECs where allowed); Scope 3 by category with documented methods.
Compute intensity: tCO2e per tonne product (GEI for CCTS), per ₹ crore turnover (BRSR), per unit floor area for buildings.
Quality: uncertainty assessment, completeness check, documentation of assumptions; internal review; management sign-off.

CCTS: submit verified GHG emission report within 4 months of FY end (31 July); respond to ACVA findings; receive/surrender CCCs via registry; plan abatement (energy efficiency, fuel switch, RE PPAs, process changes) to meet next year's GEI.

CBAM: compile installation data per EU template (direct emissions by production process, electricity consumption with factor, precursors), get verification, share with EU importer before their 30 Sep annual declaration; record carbon price paid in India for deduction claims.
Disclosure: BRSR Principle 6 (Scope 1/2 totals, intensity, Scope 3 leadership), CDP/GRI as applicable; maintain evidence files for assurance.
Improvement: set targets (SBTi-aligned where chosen), energy audits (EC Act), project pipeline, annual recalculation of base year on structural change.

records: Inventory management plan, data logs & evidence, factor sources, calculation workbooks, verification statements, CCTS monitoring plan/approvals/registry statements, CBAM data packs, BRSR extracts, target & project tracker

hazards: Inconsistent OSH data between statutory registers and BRSR (assurance findings); misstatements (SEBI action)
Missed EPR registration/targets (environmental compensation); EC Act penalties for energy audit/return defaults

BRSR Core KPI definitions: LTIFR (per million hours), fatalities, high-consequence injuries, recordable injuries, safety-related complaints; energy intensity; water intensity; waste; GHG; wages/gender; customer complaints; openness of business (trade payables concentration)

EC Act: check designated-consumer status (thresholds by sector), appoint energy manager, energy audit by accredited auditor (periodicity per notification), annual energy return (Form 1/2) to SDA/BEE; ISO 50001 recommended

EPR: register as producer/importer/brand owner/bulk consumer/generator on CPCB portals (plastic, e-waste, battery, tyre, used oil); set up collection/hand-over contracts with registered recyclers; annual returns
Supplier code of conduct and value-chain data collection (≥ 2% partners for BRSR assurance); human-rights/labour due diligence (child/forced labour, wages, OSH)

Collect and reconcile OSH data from incident registers, OSH Code annual return, ESI records; hours worked from attendance systems; ensure the same numbers appear in BRSR, annual return and insurance filings.

Environmental data: GHG (from inventory), energy (bills/meters), water (withdrawal/discharge by source), waste by type and disposal (manifests), air emissions (stack results); recycled inputs; EPR fulfilment.
Social: training hours, grievances, complaints (POSH), wages and gender metrics, contractor/migrant worker welfare evidence.
Assurance: engage practitioner; evidence packs per KPI; walkthroughs; close findings; management representation.
Disclosures: BRSR sections A–C with Core KPIs; ESG rating engagement; website publication; respond to customer ESG questionnaires (EcoVadis, CDP, CSRD data).

EPR operations: tagging of e-waste/battery/used-oil generation, storage limits, hand-over to registered recyclers with certificates, portal returns; plastic packaging accounting.

t: Fire Protection Systems – Design Basis, Testing, Maintenance & Impairment Control
purpose: Keep fire-water, sprinkler, hydrant, detection, alarm, suppression and passive fire-protection systems reliable, and control periods when they are impaired.
scope: Factories, warehouses, high-rise construction (progressive installation), tank farms (foam/cooling), data/control rooms (clean agent), battery rooms, kitchens (wet chemical), substations (CO2/water mist), labour camps (extinguishers/water).
hazards: Systems that fail on demand: dry pumps, closed valves, low water, dead batteries, blocked hydrants, painted sprinklers, impaired detectors
Unmanaged impairments during maintenance/construction → uncontrolled fire; hot work during impairment
pre: Design basis per NBC Part 4/IS/TAC/NFPA: hazard classification, water reserve (typically 2–4 h), pump set (electric + diesel + jockey), hydrant spacing, sprinkler density, detection type by area, foam for Class B, clean agent for electronics, Class D for metals; drawings and hydraulic calculations
Fire NOC and insurer requirements documented; AMC with competent agency; spares; ITM schedule (NFPA 25 / IS 15105 / IS 13039 / IS 2189 / IS 2190)

Impairment procedure: pre-planned vs emergency impairment; tags on valves/panels; notification list (fire brigade where required, insurer, site head); compensating measures (fire watch, hot-work ban, extra extinguishers, hose lines charged); restoration test
Water supply security: tank level monitoring, alternative supply/tanker tie-up; power supply to pumps on dedicated feeder/DG
steps: Weekly: diesel pump 30-min run, electric pump churn test, jockey pressure, control valve supervision (open and locked/sealed), alarm panel healthy, water level, hydrant cabinet contents.

Monthly: extinguisher visual (pressure, seal, tag), emergency lighting flick test, fire doors/closers, hydrant valve exercise sample, foam system visual, detector cleanliness, sprinkler heads not obstructed/painted/storage ≥ 450 mm below.

Quarterly: hydrant flow at remote points, main drain test (sprinklers), alarm devices audibility test, fire door inspection, gas-suppression pressure/weight check, duct/kitchen hood cleaning as needed.

Annual: pump performance (flow/pressure curve), full sprinkler/hydrant test including deluge trip, detection loop test 100% of devices, foam concentrate lab test, extinguisher service, emergency lighting 3-h duration, passive fire-stopping survey, fire-drill with system use; 5-yearly: internal pipe inspection, pressure gauge calibration, hydrostatic test of hoses; 10-yearly CO2/clean-agent cylinder hydro test; extinguisher hydro test 3–5 years.

Construction sites: install standpipe/riser as floors rise (charged within two floors of work), temporary hydrants, extinguishers per floor and at hot-work; maintain fire tender access roads; protect systems from construction damage.
Impairment: authorise on tag/log; implement compensating measures; limit duration (same shift where possible); restore and test; close log; notify.
Keep records (ITM logs) for Fire Service/insurer; trend defects; replace obsolete components; update design basis on occupancy/process change.
Train ERT on hydrant/hose drill, pump operation, panel reset, foam branch use; monthly drills.
ppe: ERT: fire kit, helmet, gloves, boots; SCBA
stop: Fire pump failed test/ unavailable without compensating measures
Hot work planned during impairment without controls
records: Design basis & drawings, Fire NOC/insurer surveys, ITM logs (weekly/monthly/quarterly/annual/5-yr), impairment log, AMC reports, drill records, defect trend

t: Cooling Towers, Water Systems & Legionella Control
purpose: Prevent Legionnaires' disease and water-system hazards (chemical dosing, drift, confined spaces) in cooling towers, evaporative condensers, hot and cold water systems and spray systems.
scope: Industrial cooling towers, HVAC towers, evaporative condensers, hot-water systems, showers in camps/plants, humidifiers, water features, firewater tanks (stagnation).
hazards: Legionella growth 20–45 °C in stagnant/biofilm water; aerosol from drift and showers; immunocompromised/older workers at risk
Biocide/acid/alkali dosing chemicals (chlorine, bromine, hypochlorite); confined-space entry into basins/tanks; falls on wet tower decks/ladders
pre: Written scheme/risk assessment: schematic of systems, dead legs identified, control measures, monitoring, roles; records for 5 years

Cooling towers: drift eliminators, accessible basins, biocide programme (oxidising + non-oxidising), corrosion/scale control, bleed-off, cleaning/disinfection at least 6-monthly (quarterly in heavy fouling), microbiological testing (TVC monthly, Legionella quarterly), action levels (Legionella ≥ 100 cfu/L review; ≥ 1,000 cfu/L immediate disinfection)
Hot/cold water: hot stored ≥ 60 °C, distributed ≥ 50 °C, cold < 20 °C; flush little-used outlets weekly; descale shower heads quarterly; TMVs maintained
Chemical dosing: bunded, labelled, SDS, PPE, eyewash; automated dosing with interlocks; no mixing of acids with hypochlorite
Confined-space procedures for basins/tanks; WAH for tower access
steps: Weekly: check tower operation, water treatment parameters (conductivity, pH, biocide residual), bleed, drift eliminators; flush infrequently used outlets.
Monthly: TVC sampling; temperature checks at sentinel taps (hot/cold); inspect tanks/tower condition; dosing equipment calibration.
Quarterly: Legionella sampling (towers; hot/cold where risk), shower-head cleaning, tower pack/basin inspection.
Six-monthly: tower cleaning & disinfection (chlorination ≥ 5–50 mg/L per method, contact time, neutralise before discharge to drain – SPCB limits), tank cleaning where sediment; review scheme.
Positive results: ≥ 1,000 cfu/L — immediate shock disinfection, re-sample, investigate; cluster of pneumonia cases — inform health authority, isolate system.
Shutdown/stagnation: drain or maintain circulation and biocide; before restart after > 1 week idle, clean/disinfect; firewater tanks on recirculation/chlorination schedule.
Chemical handling: PPE, spill kits, segregated storage; dosing room ventilation; never mix.
Records of all checks, results and actions; annual review of risk assessment; training for operators.
ppe: Gloves, goggles/face shield for chemicals, respirator (FFP3) when cleaning towers/aerosol work, harness for tower access, boots
stop: Dosing failure/biocide residual absent for > 48 h
Entry into basin without confined-space controls
records: Water-system schematics & risk assessment, treatment logs, sampling results, cleaning/disinfection certificates, dosing chemical SDS/inventory, incident/outbreak reports
